exam.title: Design and Technology Paper 1 (17/1) - October/November 2018
exam.subject: Design and Technology
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: What is the base metal used in the production of ferrous metals?
questions.explanation: Ferrous metals are those based on iron. Mild steel and cast iron are alloys made from iron, and zinc is non-ferrous.

questions.question: Which of the following is a back saw?
questions.explanation: A back saw (tenon saw) has a rigid strip of steel folded over the top of the blade to stiffen it, which is what keeps the cut straight.

questions.question: Which of the following is a factor to consider when marking out materials?
options: Use one tool on all materials
Use a blunt tool to work on materials
Ensure the use of techniques applicable on all materials
questions.explanation: Marking out sets the position of every later cut, so accuracy is the governing factor. Different materials need different marking tools, and a blunt tool gives a wide, imprecise line.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of the man-made board?
questions.explanation: Plywood is built from veneers glued with the grain of each layer at right angles to the next, so it resists bending in every direction. It uses an odd number of plies so that the two faces run the same way.

questions.question: Which of the following is the use of a try square?
questions.explanation: A try square has a fixed 90 degree blade. It is used to test that an edge is square to a face, and to mark lines square across the work.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of following the steps when bisecting line PQ?
questions.explanation: Scribe the arcs from P first (step 3), then from Q (step 4), check that they cross above and below the line (step 1), and finally join the two intersections (step 2).

questions.question: Which of the following is a shell structure?
questions.explanation: A shell structure is a hollow, thin-walled object that takes its strength from its skin, like a water tank. The ladder, chair and stove stand are frame structures built from separate members.

questions.question: A hacksaw blade cuts material on a
questions.explanation: Hacksaw teeth point away from the handle, so the blade cuts as it is pushed forward. Pressure should be released on the return stroke.

questions.question: When using a drilling machine one should
options: make sure the tie is loose.
first mark a dot punch hole.
questions.explanation: Unclamped work can be snatched round by the drill. Clamping it, and never wearing loose clothing, is the main safety rule at a drilling machine.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes efficient energy use?
options: Disable low-energy mode when using a computer
Switch on air conditioners in the afternoons
questions.explanation: Efficient use means not spending energy on work that is not being done. Appliances left idle draw power for no benefit.

questions.question: Which of the following converts rotary to linear motion?
options: A door hinged to a frame
A rip saw cutting a piece of wood
questions.explanation: A sliding gate is driven by a rotating pinion running along a rack, which turns rotary motion into motion in a straight line. A hand drill stays rotary and a hinged door swings.

questions.question: Which of the following mechanisms will make part K drop quickly?
questions.explanation: A snail or drop cam rises gradually and then falls away at a step, so the follower drops suddenly. The round and pear cams give a smooth rise and fall.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for marking a parallel line to the edge of a metal?
questions.explanation: Odd leg (jenny) calipers have one bent leg that hooks over the edge of the metal while the pointed leg scribes a line parallel to it. A marking gauge does the same job on wood.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of plastics are thermoplastics?
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics soften each time they are heated and can be reshaped. The formaldehydes, polyester and epoxy resin are thermosets, which set permanently on curing.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a shading technique?
questions.explanation: Hatching, line and tone are all ways of shading a drawing to suggest form. Contrast describes the difference between light and dark areas rather than a technique for producing them.

questions.question: What is the name of the hinge?
questions.explanation: A concealed (cup) hinge is housed in a hole bored in the door and screwed to a plate inside the cabinet, so nothing shows when the door is closed.

questions.question: What is the disadvantage of using an abrasive paper without a sanding block?
options: It is impossible to round-off edges.
It is not easy to hold the abrasive paper.
There is unevenness left on the surface.
The abrasive paper does not remove waste.
questions.explanation: Without a block the fingers press harder in some places than others, so the surface ends up hollow and uneven. The block spreads the pressure evenly.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of a PVA adhesive?
questions.explanation: PVA is a water-based emulsion: it goes on white, dries clear, and is cleaned up with water. That also means it is not water resistant.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a pre-finish?
questions.explanation: Gloss, matt and varnish describe the finished surface. A stain colours the timber and is applied before finishing, so it is not a characteristic of the finish itself.

questions.question: Why is copper used for making soldering bits?
options: It is a good conductor of electricity.
It is a good conductor of heat.
questions.explanation: The bit has to store heat and pass it quickly into the joint. Copper conducts heat better than almost any other affordable metal.

questions.question: Which tool is suitable for producing the part marked T on the wooden block?
questions.explanation: A Forstner bit cuts a clean, flat-bottomed hole and is guided by its rim rather than a centre point, so it can cut a hole that runs off the edge of the work.

questions.question: Which statement is not correct about a Working Drawing?
questions.explanation: A working drawing gives separate flat views (plan, elevation, end view) drawn to scale and dimensioned. Three-dimensional pictures are pictorial drawings.

questions.question: Which of the following will cause structural failure?
questions.explanation: Strain is the deformation caused by a load. Increase it beyond what the material can take and the structure fails. The other three make a structure safer.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to clean a brush after use in acrylic paint?
questions.explanation: Acrylic paint is water based, so brushes wash out in water provided the paint has not dried. The solvents listed are for oil-based paints.

questions.question: Quarter sawing method
questions.explanation: Quarter sawing cuts the boards so that the growth rings run roughly at right angles to the face. Such boards shrink evenly and are far less likely to cup or warp, although the method is slower and more wasteful.

questions.question: Which forces are exerted on the base of the trampoline when it is in use?
questions.explanation: The child's weight pushes the legs down, squeezing them (compression), while the mat and springs are stretched (tension).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement about the sketch?
options: XY is the same length as YZ.
XY is divided into ration of 1:5.
XY is divided into five equal parts.
questions.explanation: This is the standard construction for dividing a line into equal parts: step equal spaces along a line drawn at an angle, then project them back, which divides XY into five equal lengths.

questions.question: Which of the following is done before designing a product?
options: Establishing the need for the product
Ordering raw materials for the product
Planning the packaging of the product
Determining the quantity of the product
questions.explanation: The design process starts by identifying the need or problem. Everything else follows from the brief that the need produces.

questions.question: Which of the following shows an illustration of a chisel handle with a ferrule?
questions.explanation: A ferrule is the metal ring fitted where the blade's tang enters the handle. It stops the handle splitting when the chisel is struck.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about the eye of a ball pein hammer?
options: The wedge is always fitted along the eye.
The eye is left soft to absorb shock.
The eye is hemispherical in shape.
The eye is made from wood only.
questions.explanation: The face and the pein are hardened, but the metal around the eye is left soft so that it absorbs shock instead of cracking. The wedge is driven across the eye, not along it.

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct grip for heavy filing?
questions.explanation: For heavy filing the handle is held in one hand while the heel of the other hand presses down on the tip of the file, so that real force can be applied on the forward stroke.

questions.question: In the portfolio of an artifact, there was a statement “construction was changed”. What part of the evaluation stage is the statement?
questions.explanation: A modification records a change that was actually made to the artefact. An improvement is a change suggested for next time.

questions.question: Which of the following shows a pictorial view of the component?
questions.explanation: The symbol is a diode with two arrows pointing away from it, which marks a light emitting diode. An LED is a small coloured dome with two legs, the longer one positive.

questions.question: What is the main reason for connecting batteries in series?
questions.explanation: Cells joined in series add their voltages, so the higher voltage drives more current and delivers power faster. Joining them in parallel is what makes them last longer.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about the gear train?
options: Gear S is an idler gear.
Gear P is the driven gear.
Gear Q rotates faster than gear P.
Gear Q and gear R rotate at the same speed.
questions.explanation: P is on the motor shaft, so it is the driver, and the 20 tooth Q turns at half the speed of the 10 tooth P. Q and R share a shaft, so they must turn together.

questions.question: What is the ratio of gear P to gear Q?
questions.explanation: Gear P has 10 teeth and gear Q has 20, so the ratio is 10:20, which simplifies to 1:2. Q turns once for every two turns of P.

questions.question: Which of the following has been drawn in perspective?
questions.explanation: In a perspective drawing the receding edges converge towards a vanishing point, so the far face is drawn smaller than the near one. In isometric and oblique drawings those edges stay parallel.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes a specification of the trolley?
options: It is pushed on the floor.
It carries one book at a time as many may fall.
It is made from light material so that it moves easily.
questions.explanation: A specification states a requirement together with the reason for it, so that the finished product can be tested against it. “Easy to use” is too vague to test.

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct use of a try square on wood?
questions.explanation: The stock of the square must be held firmly against the face edge or face side of the timber, with the blade lying flat across the surface. If the stock is not pressed against the edge the line will not be square.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct plan of the block?
questions.explanation: The plan is the view looking straight down. It shows the full outline of the base, with lines where the raised portions begin and end. Hidden detail would be dashed.
